 Exhausted Trump tells Kansas crowd 'I had to come here!' at 30th rally in a month
 Connor McCrory Updated 2026년 11월 2일 월 오전 3:08 UTC 0 President Trump told Kansas supporters he 'had to come here' to help Sen. Roger Marshall win reelection -Credit:Fox News (Fox News) President Donald Trump told supporters in Kansas on Sunday that he “had to come here” to help Republican Senator Roger Marshall win reelection.
 Speaking in Salina two days before the midterm elections, Trump said he was wrapping up a cross-country campaign push with an appeal for voters to protect Republican control of Congress.
 “And I’m closing it down tonight. This is it,” an exhausted Trump said, after earlier speaking in Iowa at around 6pm ET. “I had to come here to make sure that Roger got elected. I had to do it.”

 • Donald Trump travels with gold-framed portrait of Bill Clinton on Air Force One 
 “I didn’t wanna take a chance,” Trump said. “I could have been home watching television. I’d rather be with you, believe me, I love you all.”
 The rally at Salina Regional Airport followed an appearance earlier Sunday in Dubuque, Iowa. 
 Marshall faces Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton in a contest that has drawn additional attention and visits from national Republicans.
 The rally at Salina Regional Airport followed an appearance earlier Sunday in Dubuque, Iowa -Credit:Fox News Trump also urged Kansas voters to elect Republican gubernatorial candidate Ty Masterson, repeatedly tying the candidates’ prospects to his own political standing.
 “I really want you to pretend I’m on the ballot,” Trump said.
 Advertisement
 He acknowledged the difficulties presidents’ parties typically encounter in midterm elections but insisted Republicans could overcome that pattern with strong turnout.
 “But all I’m asking you to do is one thing, get out and vote, because if you do, we’re gonna have a tremendous success,” he said.
 The Kansas appearance followed several changes to the president’s schedule. A Saturday rally was initially canceled in favor of a telephone event before campaign officials announced the Sunday visit.
 Despite describing the evening as the end of his campaign travels, Trump told the crowd he had enjoyed the demanding itinerary.
 “I mean, what we’ve done, we have travelled far and wide,” he said. “And we’ve campaigned and I’ve enjoyed it.”
 His remarks moved between election appeals, attacks on Democrats and observations about an aircraft visible from the rally.
 “And by the way, I’m looking at that plane, is that beautiful?” Trump asked, before discussing its red, white and blue paint scheme and gold stripe.
 He also discussed the Kansas City Chiefs, saying organizers had timed his appearance to follow their football game.
 Returning to Tuesday’s elections, Trump urged supporters to deliver victories for Marshall, Masterson and other Republicans.
 “We want to have a tremendous victory on Tuesday night,” he said. “We wanna watch Roger and Ty and everybody with a big night because they deserve it.”
